I've never really been interested in detective stories before, but a lot of old writers and philosophers speak really highly of them so I thought i'd check out the genre! Any know a good place to start?
Where to start with Detective Novels?
Conan Doyle's "A Study in Scarlet" is a good start. first novel featuring Sherlock Holmes
That sounds like a good base line. I'm only really familiar with the BBC Sherlock so it'd be interesting to see how that character has evolved culturally.

I really liked the Robot series by Isaac Asimov. Detective Scifi novels, and a nice tie in if you ever read the foundation series. The novels are about the 3 laws of robotics; "A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm. A robot must obey orders given it by human beings except where such orders would conflict with the First Law. A robot must protect its own existence as long as such protection does not conflict with the First or Second Law." The books explore the flaws in these laws through detectives Elijah Bailey and R Olivaw. Its interesting how these laws create contradictions and seemingly impossible situations,
I actually just started reading the Foundation Series! Could I read them in tandem or should I finish Foundation first?
No real order is needed, there's a small cameo at the end of the Foundation series, no difference what order you read the series. Sounds like the Robot series would be right up your alley.

Dashiell Hammet was one of the early detective story writers. His stories and characters are very good.

My personal favorites are the 87th precinct stories by Ed McBain. You get a real sense of procedure and get to know a large cast of characters and how crimes are solved from the 50s to modern day. They are my go to novels when I have nothing to read. They are written well and the stories are interesting.
Awesome, that sounds like exactly what i'm looking for. I'm really in the market for some fun, intelligent, summer reads.
Agatha Christie, And Then There Were None.
I could read any Agatha Christie at any time. I also really like Dorothy Sayers.
My first detective novel was ''Murder on the Orient Express'' and I have loved every other Agatha Christie book I have read since.

Another person mentioned And Then There Were None. I'd definitely add another Agatha Christie novel.. Try The Murder of Roger Ackroyd for an absolutely fantastic murder mystery.

I enjoyed The Big Sleep and The Maltese Falcon for more gritty detective novels. If I think of any others, I'll pass them along!

If you want something modern and a little bit scifi try The Last Policeman by Ben H. Winters. It's the first book in a series about a policeman doing detective work after the world has found out that there's a life ending meteor heading for Earth.

Do Androids Dream of Electric by Isaac Asimov is another great scifi about a man hunting down a rogue android.

If you enjoy urban fantasy The Dresden Files series by Jim Butcher is great. A wizard working with the police to hunt down things that go bump in the night.

Another great scifi is Leviathan Wakes. It's the first book in a series. A detective helps a space captain solve a mystery in space. The rest of the books lose the detective feel, but are still great scifi.

I know there's alot of cross genre works in my list, but they all contain the detective story element. If you're into scifi or fantasy any of them would be great ways to cross the bridge into more traditional detective stories.

• The Bat - Jo Nesbo
  • Harry Bosch - Michael Connelly
  • The Camel Club - David Baldacci (possibly not a detective book but an investigation)
  • The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo - Stieg Larsson (investigation again).
